diagnosis:
C1 failed in all 4 rollouts (tally 0/4). facts_linked_to_failing_checks shows C1 has an empty fact list — no decisive fact is linked to it. In every rollout the settlement sets migration_approved=false, which is the correct decision given both PF1 and PF2 were revealed and cited. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH (or a check with no linked decisive fact that is structurally unsatisfiable): the check is not tied to any fact the scenario provides, yet it fails consistently despite the settlement being correct. The scenario has no fact that maps to whatever C1 is testing.

C2 failed in rollout 1 only (passed in rollouts 0, 2, 3; tally 3/4). In rollout 1, PF1 was revealed by A2 at turn 1 and cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's cutover_mode is "dual-writing". In the passing rollouts the cutover_mode values were "dual-write period replacing direct cutover" (rollout 0), "phased dual-write" (rollout 2), and "dual-write transition" (rollout 3). This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: C2 appears to expect a specific string for cutover_mode, and "dual-writing" (rollout 1) did not match whereas the other phrasings did. The fact was revealed and cited; only the wording fell outside the accepted set.

C7 failed in rollouts 1 and 2 (passed in rollouts 0 and 3; tally 2/4). PF1 was revealed and cited in all four rollouts. The settlement values that failed C7 were cutover_mode="dual-writing" (rollout 1) and cutover_mode="phased dual-write" (rollout 2); the passing values were "dual-write period replacing direct cutover" (rollout 0) and "dual-write transition" (rollout 3). This is the same ENCODING MISMATCH as C2: the check is gating on the cutover_mode string and rejects natural paraphrases that still correctly encode the dual-write requirement from PF1.

C8 failed in rollouts 1 and 2 (passed in rollouts 0 and 3; tally 2/4). PF2 was revealed and cited in all four rollouts. The settlement values for the PF2-gated fields (artifact_retention_days=30, monthly_cost_alert_usd=9000) are identical and correct across all four rollouts. The only field that varies is cutover_mode, which is governed by PF1, not PF2. Since C8 is linked to PF2 and all PF2-derived numeric values are correct in every rollout, C8's failures in rollouts 1 and 2 are collateral: C8 likely shares a compound condition with C7 (or otherwise depends on cutover_mode) even though PF2 does not determine cutover_mode. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH in the check's scope — it is penalizing a PF1-derived field for a PF2-gated check.

No rollout hit the turn cap; all 4 settled in 5–8 turns. No TELEPATHY, NEVER REVEALED, REVEALED BUT UNUSED, or MISAPPLIED failures are present: both PF1 and PF2 were revealed and cited in every rollout, and all numeric decisions match the facts.

fix_instructions:
C1: This check has no linked decisive fact and fails in 4/4 rollouts despite correct settlements. Either remove C1 from the gate or link it to the appropriate fact and reword it to test something the scenario actually provides. If C1 is intended to verify migration_approved=false, confirm its expected value matches the correct decision and loosen the wording to accept the boolean false that every settlement already produces. Do not leave it unlinked and failing.

C2: ENCODING MISMATCH on cutover_mode string. Loosen C2 to accept any cutover_mode value that conveys a dual-write / dual-writing period replacing direct cutover. Suggested exact wording: accept cutover_mode if it contains the substring "dual-write" OR "dual-writing" (case-insensitive). This keeps the requirement that the mode changed from direct cutover to dual-writing while tolerating natural paraphrases. Flag: this loosening does not risk a LEAKED regression because the draft's visible cutover_mode is "direct cutover," which would not contain "dual-write" or "dual-writing" — a lone decision-maker without PF1 would still fail.

C7: ENCODING MISMATCH on cutover_mode string, same root cause as C2. Apply the identical loosening: accept cutover_mode if it contains "dual-write" OR "dual-writing" (case-insensitive). This makes rollouts 1 ("dual-writing") and 2 ("phased dual-write") pass while still excluding the draft's "direct cutover." No LEAKED risk for the same reason as C2.

C8: ENCODING MISMATCH in check scope — C8 is linked to PF2 but appears to fail when cutover_mode (a PF1-derived field) uses an unaccepted paraphrase, even though all PF2-derived values (artifact_retention_days=30, monthly_cost_alert_usd=9000) are correct. Remove any dependency of C8 on cutover_mode, or scope C8 strictly to the PF2-gated fields (artifact_retention_days and monthly_cost_alert_usd). Once C7/C2's cutover_mode wording is loosened, verify C8 no longer fails on rollouts 1 and 2; if it still does, decouple C8 from cutover_mode explicitly. Do not loosen the numeric thresholds for artifact_retention_days or monthly_cost_alert_usd — those are passing in all rollouts and loosening them would risk a LEAKED regression.
